source: NLSY79 public release 1979-2022 (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics), all rounds; respondents born 1957-1964; first marriages begun January 1981 to 2022, followed to the last interview (2022 at the latest)
target: Annual rate of legal divorce ending a FIRST marriage, per marriage-year counted from the wedding month; widowhood censored (Poisson rate, not a probability). Separation alone is not an event.
population: U.S. men and women born 1957-64 in their first marriage, wedded between 1981 and 2022 at ages 16-63 (central 99%: 18-55); the respondent reports on themself and the spouse listed in the household roster
weights: NLSY79 sampling weight from the last interview before the wedding (normalised to mean 1) times exposure
entry: Delayed entry: a marriage joins the risk set at the first interview after the wedding (median 8 months), when the spouse is observed; marriage years still count from the wedding month

inputs.marriage_years: completed years since the wedding at the start of the year being scored (0 = first year)
inputs.age_at_marriage: respondent's age in years at the wedding
inputs.wedding_year: calendar year of the wedding; 1981-2022 in the data, few after 2000, so the app should hold it at the upper support bound and say so
inputs.afqt: AFQT percentile (2006 revision), ASVAB taken in 1980
inputs.rotter: Rotter locus-of-control score 4-16 (1979; higher = more external)
inputs.delinquency: number of 18 delinquent acts reported for the past year in 1980 (0-18)
inputs.income_percentile: weighted percentile of total net family income in the calendar year before the pre-wedding interview, among everyone interviewed that round
inputs.spouse_age_at_marriage: spouse's age at the wedding (roster age at the first post-wedding interview minus the time since the wedding)
inputs.race: Hispanic, Black, Non-Black non-Hispanic (NLSY79 screener cohort)
inputs.own_education: highest grade completed at the pre-wedding interview: <12, 12, 13-15, 16+ years
inputs.enrolled: enrolled in school or college at the pre-wedding interview
inputs.mother_education: mother's highest grade (1979 report), same bands
inputs.father_education: father's highest grade (1979 report), same bands
inputs.family_at_14: who the respondent lived with at 14 (1979 report)
inputs.attendance: religious attendance in the past year, 1982 report if that interview preceded the wedding, else 1979
inputs.poverty: family poverty status at the pre-wedding interview
inputs.region: Census region at the pre-wedding interview
inputs.urban: urban/rural residence at the pre-wedding interview
inputs.premarital_birth: respondent had a child born before the wedding month
inputs.cohabiting_before: a partner (relationship code 33) was in the household at the pre-wedding interview
inputs.lived_with_parents: a parent or step-parent was in the household at the pre-wedding interview
inputs.spouse_in_household: a spouse was listed in the household at the first post-wedding interview (Yes for any couple scored now)
inputs.spouse_education: spouse's highest grade at the first post-wedding interview, same bands
inputs.spouse_worked: spouse worked in the calendar year before the first post-wedding interview
inputs.afqt_missing: Observed/Missing flag (Missing: not tested); the app sets it from whether afqt is given
inputs.delinquency_missing: Observed/Missing flag for delinquency (fewer than 15 of 18 items answered)
inputs.age_pair: age band + " | " + spouse age band, bands <20, 20-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35+ (spline_pairs model only)

timing.pre_wedding_round: last interview strictly before the wedding month (median 7 months before): own schooling, enrolment, family income, poverty, region, urban, household roster
timing.fixed_early: 1979: family at 14, parents' schooling, religion raised, attendance, Rotter; 1980: Rosenberg, delinquency, ASVAB (AFQT); 1982: attendance. Every wedding in the sample is in January 1981 or later, so all of these precede it; the 1982 answer is used only if that interview preceded the wedding.
timing.spouse: household roster at the first interview after the wedding (median 8 months after), which is also when the marriage enters the risk set
timing.cross_round: wedding and divorce months from the cross-round marital history (MOBG1M/YRBG1M, MOEN1M/YREN1M); birth months of children (C#DOB) for premarital births

abstain: a previously married respondent (first marriages only)
weddings before 1981 or at ages outside the support
any profile above the ood abstain_above_percentile

ablation.block: age and timing (age at marriage, wedding year)

population_reference.method: Held-out predicted probability that the first marriage ends in divorce within 5, 10, 20 and 30 years of the wedding (1 - exp(-sum of predicted annual rates)), from the gradient_boosting model, averaged over 3 repeats of person-grouped 5-fold cross-validation (every marriage is scored only by models that never saw it); NLSY79 weights from the pre-wedding round; quantiles of the weighted distribution; cells with fewer than 100 unweighted marriages are not published; Unknown levels are omitted. Divorce only: deaths are not modelled, and 30 years is a projection for weddings after 1992.

cells.value: Several times a year or less

partner_distribution.source: Spouse listed in the NLSY79 household roster at the first interview after the wedding (respondent report); age at the wedding, highest grade completed in coarse bands

ood.method: squared Mahalanobis distance on the model inputs; percentile against held-out people (5 person folds)

attendance: Several times a year or less

models_extended.label: Additive spline Poisson, current inputs + all new blocks

heldout.evaluation: train_first_marriage.py person folds (5 x 3); paired person bootstrap (1000)

models_extended_note: Held-out comparison of richer inputs (2026-10-20, extended_predictors.py). Not scored by the app until the form asks for them. Blocks whose held-out difference had a 95% CI above zero: none.

inputs_extended.race_detail: Hispanic / Black (screener) / Asian or Pacific Islander origin / American Indian origin (overstated in 1979 per NLS) / White and other non-Black non-Hispanic
inputs_extended.family_at_14_detail: who the respondent lived with at 14 (FAM-7): Both parents / Mother and stepfather / Father and stepmother / Mother only / Father only / Relatives / Other. The reason a parent was absent was not asked.
inputs_extended.attendance6: religious attendance, six answers: Not at all / Infrequently / Once a month / 2-3 times a month / Once a week / More than once a week
inputs_extended.religion_1979: religious affiliation in 1979: None / Catholic / Baptist / Protestant / Jewish / Other
inputs_extended.occupation_group: current or last job before the wedding, Census major group (or No job reported)
inputs_extended.net_worth_before_k: family net wealth before the wedding, $1,000s (nominal), -50..500; median-imputed when not measured
inputs_extended.net_worth_measured: Yes if a net-wealth interview (1985 onward) preceded the wedding, else Not measured before wedding
